title: Optimal Control to Minimize Dissipation and Fluctuations in Open Quantum Systems Beyond Slow and Rapid Regimes
summary: Optimal control is a central problem in quantum thermodynamics. When minimizing dissipated work and work fluctuations defined via the two-point measurement scheme in open quantum systems, existing approaches largely focus on the rapid- and slow-driving limits, leaving the behavior at intermediate timescales elusive. In this work, by numerically optimizing the driving protocols, we demonstrate that the open quantum systems exhibit distinct optimal structures not captured by the conventional limits.
